stem: Ishaan hangs a wet handkerchief on a sunny clothesline. He also leaves an identical wet handkerchief folded inside a closed cup indoors.

parts.text: Which claim about drying is correct?

options.text: The handkerchief on the sunny clothesline dries faster because more surface is exposed and the air is warmer.
With equal wetness, the handkerchief in the closed cup dries faster because the air there is more humid.
Neither handkerchief can dry until the water reaches its boiling point.
The folded handkerchief in the cup dries faster because the cup is smaller than the clothesline.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: Water evaporates faster when more surface is open to air and when the air is warmer and less humid; it need not boil to evaporate.

teacher.key_rationale: More exposed surface and warmer, drier air speed evaporation. Humid closed air slows drying. Water can evaporate well below boiling. Cup size alone does not make the folded cloth dry faster.
